q-329817.problem:
$$ {x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}12t \\ 0\end{aligned}] $$ Consider the system of differential equations. Using the method of variation of parameters, the general solution of the equation can be written in the form
$x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+\,\,$ {{field-1}} .
$-12t-6$
q-329817.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} & 2{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}12t \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-2t}\cdot {e}^{t}-2{e}^{t}\cdot 2{e}^{-2t}}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & -2{e}^{t} \\ -2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{t}}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & -2{e}^{t} \\ -2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -2{e}^{2t} \\ -2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =-\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -2{e}^{2t} \\ -2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}12t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4t{e}^{2t} \\ 8t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}-4t{e}^{2t} \\ 8t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int -4t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int 8t{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=-4t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=-4\,\text{d}t$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -4t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t & =(-4t)\cdot \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}-\int \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}\cdot (-4\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-2t{e}^{2t}+\int 2{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =-2t{e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t} \\  & ={e}^{2t}(1-2t).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=8t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=8\,\text{d}t$ and $v=-{e}^{-t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -4t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t & =8t\cdot (-{e}^{-t})-\int -{e}^{-t}\cdot 8\,\text{d}t \\  & =-8t{e}^{-t}+\int 8\,{e}^{-t}\text{d}t \\  & =-8t{e}^{-t}-8{e}^{2t} \\  & =-8{e}^{-t}(1+t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} & 2{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t}(1-2t) \\ -8{e}^{-t}(1+t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(1-2t)-16(1+t) \\ 2(1-2t)-8(1+t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-18t-15 \\ -12t-6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
